events.title: CVE-2025-39682: Linux Kernel Linux Kernel Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability
events.summary: A Linux kernel flaw lets a zero-length TLS record bypass normal checks, potentially causing incorrect handling of subsequent TLS data. The issue targets end-of-life or end-of-service kernel versions, and users are advised to stop using them or upgrade.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and is listed in the KEV, indicating active exploitation. It could allow attackers to manipulate TLS processing, potentially leading to data corruption or denial of service.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2025-39682 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-09-18, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-09-21.
CVE-2025-39682 is rated 9.8 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2025-39682 being exploited in the next 30 days at 2.9%.
A fix for Kernel (Linux) is published in 6.1.149, 6.6.103, 6.12.44 and 6.16.4, per CVE-2025-39682.

events.title: CVE-2025-39964: Linux Kernel Linux Kernel Race Condition Vulnerability
events.summary: Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistencies in the socket's internal state.

events.title: CVE-2026-53266: Linux Kernel Linux Kernel Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability
events.summary: Linux Kernel contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ebtables SNAT target which allows an ARP sender hardware address rewrite to write directly into a nonlinear socket-buffer fragment backed by a splice-imported file page. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-53266 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-09-18, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-09-21.
